summary.headline: Zee Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 789 million (4.1% margin) as advertising dropped 11% YoY, while ZEE5 revenue rose 58% to INR 4,571 million.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was weighed down by an 11% YoY decline in advertising revenue, attributed to the Middle East conflict hitting April and May, and by a 15% rise in operating costs from FIFA 2026 marketing and new sports channel launches. Subscription revenue grew 16% YoY, and ZEE5 revenue grew 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million, though the digital business posted only INR 44 million EBITDA. Linear network share reached 20% (17.9% for the quarter through week 24), and PAT was INR 743 million. Management said significant FIFA revenue and cost will flow through in Q2, and it declined to give full-year EBITDA margin guidance.

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million, with profitable growth for the third consecutive quarter, but EBITDA only INR 44 million after higher FIFA and Bullet marketing spend. 38 shows and movies released in the quarter, including 15 originals, across 7 languages.

segments.name: Linear broadcast
segments.commentary: All-time high network share of around 20%; quarterly share of 17.9%, up 110 bps YoY (data only through week 24 as BARC stopped publishing). Zee TV led prime time for 32+ consecutive weeks; Zee Cinema led movie genre at 27% viewership in week 22.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Declined 11% YoY on Middle East conflict in April and May; June saw green shoots after FIFA rights, with advertisers engaging on premium sponsorships.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: 54 billion total video views and over 177 million YouTube subscribers; catalogue of over 20,000 songs. Management described profitability as healthy.

segments.name: Studios (other sales and services)
segments.commentary: Other sales and services up 17% YoY; studios released 9 movies (4 Hindi, 5 other languages).

segments.name: Sports
segments.commentary: Secured FIFA digital and broadcast rights until 2034 (39 events, 38 still to go), plus Bundesliga and Serie A. Four Unite8 sports channels launched in June 2026. FIFA reach exceeded 400 million, with around 83% of FIFA viewership live on ZEE5.

guidance_outlook: No full-year EBITDA margin guidance given, citing market uncertainty.
Significant portion of FIFA revenue and cost expected in Q2 FY27 versus Q1; subscription revenue on accrual basis to see significant boost in Q2.
Digital growth momentum expected to continue in Q2 as FIFA gains accrue.
Management cautiously optimistic on advertising, citing market share gains, festive season and easing West Asia conflict.
Linear subscription price hikes to be considered at next NTO cycle, expected around February 2027.
capex_capacity: Heavy past capex at technology centre flowing through amortisation; management said current D&A run rate is within a reasonable range and not expected to significantly affect results.
Inventory increase largely due to FIFA rights outflows in Q1, which will flow through P&L in Q2.
demand_pricing: Advertising weak in April-May; June improved with FIFA sponsorships. Management views ad recovery as dependent on festive season, market share gains and West Asia de-escalation.
ZEE5 renewals said to be holding up beyond FIFA; language packs aiding subscription growth (no numbers disclosed).
B2C subscribers more than doubled in the quarter, partly FIFA-driven; B2B deals under discussion but not disclosed.
Sports rights costs are high versus regular content; management stressed selective buying and audience-led value.

qa_highlights.question: When will sports turn sustainably profitable, and will premium advertisers stay post-FIFA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sports will be run prudently to reach sustained profitability, with no date given. Some marquee advertisers may exit after sports, but some will stay if delivered value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising and the 12/18-month timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company wrote to the regulator seeking clarification with no response yet and has appealed to the Securities Appellate Tribunal. Management hopes for a quick resolution; preferential allotment approval is valid for one year but the matter is sub judice.

qa_highlights.question: How is the music business accounted for and is a demerger planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal transfer pricing governs music and digital P&Ls, and ZEE5 pays for music. Additional disclosures are being worked on. Demerger has been considered but is not being pursued absent a corporate action.

qa_highlights.question: How were FIFA rights payments structured and how much hits Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost value was not disclosed; payments are staggered over 8 years with a higher amount for the 2030 World Cup. A significant portion of FIFA revenue and cost lands in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Star arbitration?
qa_highlights.answer: Hearings held in July; final submissions due in about 1 to 1.5 months, with an outcome possibly in Q3 FY27. Further hearings are possible but not known.

risks_watch: Advertising recovery depends on festive season and West Asia; ad revenue fell 11% YoY in Q1.
Sustainability of FIFA-driven subscriber gains and content amortisation costs once the tournament ends.
Fundraising timeline under regulatory review and pending appeal at the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
Star arbitration outcome expected possibly in Q3 FY27.
Premium advertisers acquired for FIFA may not remain after the event.
Music business structure and disclosures remain unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital and sports strategy but cautious on advertising and margins, which management repeatedly tied to market uncertainty. Management declined to give margin guidance and withheld several figures (FIFA cost, language-pack mix, B2B deals) as confidential, and deflected fundraising and music questions as sub judice or undecided.

financial_highlights.value: INR 22.1 billion (cash INR 4.4bn, FDs/treasury INR 5.9bn, mutual funds INR 11.8bn)

key_quotes: For us, value delivery will take precedent over pursuing expensive properties, enabling us to build a differentiated and sustainable offering.
Advertisement revenue during the quarter remained muted, primarily due to external headwinds.
I will not be in a position to give you a guidance on the EBITDA margin for the year.
We have thought about the demerger of the music business, but right now, there is no strategic reason for us to demerge the business outward.

adds.what: 4 Unite8 sports channels launched June 2026 (no capex figure given)

growth.why: Q1 ad revenue fell 11% YoY and EBITDA margin was 4.1%, offset by ZEE5 revenue up 58% and subscription up 16%, with no full-year guidance given and no new capacity beyond the launched Unite8 channels.
